programme: RFXAP drives the RFX/CIITA MHC class-II antigen-presentation module (its own target list is essentially the HLA-DR/DP/DQ/DM/DO locus plus CIITA); PRDM1/BLIMP1 sits downstream as the classical repressor of CIITA-driven MHC-II and of the PAX5/BCL6 germinal-centre programme, pushing cells toward effector/plasma fates while also carrying TBX21 and IFNG among its targets; TBX21/T-bet runs the Th1/cytotoxic-effector arm (IFNG, CXCR3, IL2RB, STAT4, SOCS1/3, HAVCR2, CD8A); EBF1 is the B-lineage commitment factor (PAX5, CD19, CD79A, VPREB1, IGLL1, BCR, FOXO1); ID2 is EBF1/E-protein's canonical antagonist, blocking B-lymphopoiesis and instead favoring NK/ILC and terminal CD8-effector differentiation; and MAFB carries macrophage/TAM differentiation (CCL2, C1QA, TNFSF11, MMP13). Together these five factors reconstruct the lineage-decision tree (antigen presentation, Th1, B, NK/effector, macrophage) that generates a solid tumour's immune contexture.
role_in_a: In colorectal cancer this maps directly onto documented biology: RFXAP/CIITA-driven HLA class II regulation tracks CD4+ T cell infiltration (25445815), TBX21 marks the Th1/cytotoxic compartment across several CRC immune-profiling studies (42230505, 42112839, 42433376) and also has a reported tumour-suppressive, metastasis-restraining arm (39744435), PRDM1 is described as a hub of immune differentiation and epigenetic repression in CRC, including a CX3CR1+ effector CD8 subset and regulatory B cell epigenetics (42396452, 41929510, 41949720), EBF1 appears in CRC stroma reprogramming cancer-associated fibroblasts (39002521), and MAFB reprogramming of tumour-associated macrophages modulates checkpoint-inhibitor efficacy (41692233). ID2's only CRC citation here is about mutagenesis, not its lineage function.
role_in_b: No paper in this record places any of the six carrying factors in kidney papillary cell carcinoma, and Open Targets records no association for RFXAP, TBX21 or MAFB there (ID2, EBF1 and PRDM1 do have OT percentiles). By extension of their canonical immunology, the same factors would be expected to run the same antigen-presentation/T/B/NK/macrophage lineage decisions on whatever leukocyte infiltrate a papillary RCC tumour recruits, but that is an extrapolation from general tumour-immunology, not an observation in this material — and papillary RCC is generally reported as a comparatively less T-cell/immune-infiltrated tumour than clear-cell RCC, which is the RCC subtype most of the checkpoint/TAM literature concerns.
shared_axis: Both are epithelial solid tumours whose bulk expression is shaped by infiltrating leukocytes; a network built from patient samples will pick up whichever transcription factors partition those leukocytes into antigen-presenting, Th1, B, NK/effector and macrophage states. The most parsimonious reading is convergence on this generic tumour-infiltrate lineage module in two immunologically distinct cancers, rather than a disease-specific pathway unique to the colorectal/kidney-papillary pairing.
reasoning: The module is coherent and nameable from well-established TF biology (RFXAP-CIITA, PRDM1-CIITA repression, TBX21 Th1, EBF1-ID2 B-vs-NK antagonism, MAFB macrophage fate), and tumour immune infiltration is textbook-documented separately for both colorectal and kidney cancers, so the connection follows without being a stated fact about this specific pair. But every retrieved citation places these factors in CRC only; the RCC side rests entirely on general immunology rather than on anything retrieved, and the 266 comparisons trace back to only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the recurrence count overstates independent replication.
support: 25445815 (HLA class II regulatory mutations associate with CD4 T cell infiltration in CRC, i.e. RFXAP's programme); 42230505, 42112839, 42433376 (TBX21/Th1-axis genes studied across CRC T cell subsets); 39744435 (TBX21 restrains CRC metastasis via a separate signalling arm); 42396452, 41929510, 41949720 (PRDM1 in CRC immune differentiation, CD8 effector subsets, regulatory B cell epigenetics); 39002521 (EBF1 axis in CRC cancer-associated fibroblasts); 41692233 (MAFB reprograms CRC tumour-associated macrophages for checkpoint efficacy). None found for Kidney_Papillary_Cell_Carcinoma or for any joint mechanism.
how_to_falsify: In matched TCGA-COAD/READ and TCGA-KIRP cohorts, test whether RFXAP/CIITA-MHCII, TBX21, PRDM1, EBF1, ID2 and MAFB expression actually segregate into the expected antigen-presenting/Th1/B/NK/macrophage compartments in papillary RCC (e.g. by deconvolution or single-cell data) the way they do in CRC. If papillary RCC tumours show minimal or discordant expression of this module (low overall leukocyte fraction, no separable B vs NK/effector signal via EBF1/ID2, no TAM signal via MAFB), the shared-programme account is wrong and the cross-disease concordance more likely reflects a network-inference artifact than shared immune biology.
caveats: Colorectal vs kidney is an anatomically and embryologically distinct pairing with no obvious shared clinical axis. The 266 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the supported_in fractions reflect repeated subgroup splits of a small underlying sample, not 266 independent replications. The single-view exclusion list (GMEB1, KLF11, COPS5, BATF3, ZMIZ1, PAX9, APEX1, RAX, NFATC1, HOXD9, FOXI1, FOXL1) shows this module survived broad cross-subgroup recurrence rather than being driven by one idiosyncratic patient group; no tissue-generic exclusion list was supplied for this pair. Retrieval was CRC-heavy and completely silent for kidney papillary carcinoma for every carrying factor — per the task's own rule, that silence is a fact about the literature/query, not evidence the connection is novel or absent.
